title: Worship in Spirit and Truth
english: With a mind fixed on praising the Source of all things (Ps 65:1b,2). The shout is a voice of those having triumphed over those having been conquered, being sent up insignificantly so that the sound of the voice might be passed on to the utmost extent. For since, by the grace of God, through Jesus having tasted every death, the dead are raised, the devil having been destroyed—he who held the power of death—it is commanded not just a part of the earth but the whole earth to shout to God, as the righteous and unrighteous dead are being raised everywhere.

And regarding the resurrection of repentance, it is fitting for the whole earth to shout, the place being called the place of repentance for the men of the whole earth. For it is said regarding the fallen: 'Not everyone who falls is not raised' (Prov 24:16), and regarding the whole church from among the Gentiles, the Lord says: 'Arise, my neighbor, that you may stand through repentance and be with Him.' When the shout of the voice has occurred on behalf of those defeated, those having been freed from the enemies are commanded to confess to God the cause of the victory, praising Him and singing in His name; but not as they happened to be, but gloriously; for He says, 'He shall praise His glory.' And this happens when the one singing makes the praise a fitting practice; for it is fitting for the well-disposed to praise. Therefore, the unworthy is forbidden from doing this, as it is not beautiful for a beautiful mind to be in the mouth of a sinner.

It is not always necessary to take falsehood upon word and glory (Ps 65:3). For the voice itself lies even regarding the protesting of the purpose. By this meaning, the enemies of God lied, even though they were not able to withstand Him in any measure. For through the multitude of divine works being done by Jesus, a divine power being manifested in the things occurring, the Jews, wishing to hate, thought Jesus to be a mere man and were lying, saying, 'By Beelzebul, ruler of the demons, He casts out the demons,' even though the works were demonstrating that these are greater than any created thing; therefore, for their understanding, the Savior said to them: 'Do not believe me; believe the works, so that you may know what I am in the Father and the Father is in me.'
With the Savior having arrived, the shadow of the Law finally took its leave (Ps 65:4); therefore, nothing is hastened to be performed in the temple in Jerusalem regarding the [rites] of God.

Worship, being done in spirit and truth, does not prevent a worshiper of God from doing this in any place. For they shall worship Him, and whoever does appropriate things for worshiping God from that place, for the word says: 'Worship Him and sing praises to Him' (Ps 65:5,6). And they do this blamelessly, when Your presence is called upon them; for God has necessarily brought the 'Sing praises to Your name' (Ps 65:6) to pass.

Come, O lovers of learning, and see the works of God accomplished in faithful men, being carried out not by human will but by the will of God. For how is it possible to accomplish poverty and lack, unless the will of God is working them? And what God is He, who provides the power to endure these things? He, whose life is tossed and troubled, changed the unruffled into dry land, casting the word of fire upon the earth, all moisture drying up, so that those coming from wickedness into virtue and from unbelief into faith might have the sea turned into a path to walk upon. The symbol of this is iconographically depicted by the faith of the apostle Peter, walking upon the sea toward the Savior.

But the river is the word, strengthened by Greek wisdom and art, blocking the way to the land leading to holiness. But He also turned this one, mocking the wise in their craftiness, and made a firm footing for those traveling toward holiness. And the things said against those who interrupt the divinity are a refutation. For no other god divided the Red Sea and performed the tremendous powers in the Gospels. For Jesus saved the people in Egypt, as it says in an apostolic epistle.

Having become by work and disposition, the sea and the river were turned into dry land so that one might cross as a path, traveling unhindered from wickedness and impiety toward virtue and piety. We rejoice in Him who made the difficult easy, God reigning kingly over the age and those in it, as He separates from the evil in it those who have believed, according to what was said: 'How He shall deliver us from the present evil age' (2 Thess 3:3). And it is possible to take the age that is testing, from the spoken word, in agreement with the Lord.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Spiritual Sacrifices and the Soul's Trials
english: through the power of his joined kingdom

To burn and to move the soul hotly, it is called fire; but by another thought, it is called water because of its drowning and suffocating those who do not bear these things bravely. This, having been passed through by the cooperation of God, comes forth for the refreshment of life, hoping for rewards upon them. And since the beginnings and the progress belong to our practical efforts, while the ends belong to the gift of God—giving to themselves the passing through fire and water, while writing the cause of the end to God—what are the circumstances of fire and water? It is shown by the prophet Isaiah saying from the face of God: 'Fear not, for I am with you; and if you pass through fire, flame shall not burn you; and if you pass through water, rivers shall not overwhelm you' (Isa 43:2). 'I will enter into your house with burnt offerings, and I will pay my vows' (Ps 65:13-14). Before the arrival of the Savior, the sacrifices according to the law were offered; but entering into the house of God (which is the church) spiritually, one performs perfect and complete virtues through burnt offerings, giving to this burnt offering compatible [virtues] and paying the vows his lips sent.

The previously interpreted spiritual burnt offerings are found to be flourishing and marrow-filled, which are offered up not for the sake of another but for God. These things, indeed, are offered up in the manner that is necessary, with supplications; and this is signified by the very name of incense. 'Let my prayer be directed as incense before you' (Ps 141:2). And the offering is not made by incense alone, but also by rams. The rams are movements and fragrances, having their beginning from the incense of the soul. Along with the marrow-filled burnt offerings, the incense, and the rams, there is promised to open a cry with snow, perhaps through a bull performing a living sacrifice to God, the unique body; for the animal is a farmer, having an analogy with the body from the creation out of the earth. The snows are the works and words of repentance; for the ram is offered concerning sin. 'Without tongue and its offering, according to that which is kept silent in thought, you shall increase' (Ps 65:17). It is possible to take the verse with such understanding: 'If I had observed iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened' (Ps 65:18).

title: The Way and the Salvation of God
english: This is what is taken by Paul: 'I do no favors to myself, but I am not justified by this; for God sees the injustice in me, and my heart does not perceive it.' To this, who will understand the transgressions? 'Cleanse me from my secret sins' (Ps 65:20). This has happened to me, not so much because of my sinlessness, but because of His mercy, which did not depart from me, the divine mercy not withdrawing because of not asking good things, but things pleasant and sweet to men.

The Psalm (Ps 66) is not in need of much interpretation because it has a clear mind. For it proclaims the becoming-man of the Word of God, and the saving appearance, and the salvation of all the Gentiles; 'Unto the end it is written.' And since the accomplished things are not human works, it is not written in panegyrics or praises, but in hymns; for to hymn is God's, but to panegyrize through praise is of men. Therefore, pay attention, the divine hymn, being a Psalm of song, and declaring the deeds of the Savior and their greatest contemplation, is arranged not by chance but in a beautiful containing number; for the number 26 has perfection in both units and tens.

Men are filled with mercies and blessings when the face of Him shines upon those wishing to experience this (Ps 66:2). And the face of the Creator of all shines when the character of His subsistence, having become man, arrives and reveals Himself to those worthy, as He says concerning the one who keeps His commandments, 'I will manifest myself to him.' Since this exists, the one saying these things is an image of the invisible God; the one approaching Him with a pure mind sees the Father; for He says, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9). In this way, the divine face having appeared, those being benefited are pitied and are blessed with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus.

Your face having appeared, the way leading to You toward the Father is known (Ps 66:3). And who is this who said, 'I am the way and no one comes to the Father except through me' (John 14:6)? In agreement with the being known on the earth the way of God and His salvation, not...

The way of the Lord will be known among all the nations when all flesh is filled with the sight of the salvation of God. It is possible, when the way of God is made known in the land, to receive his commandments, according to 'I have run according to your commandments' (Ps 66:4).

Salvation, being in harmony with this way, is what has come to be known by all the nations and is what has come to provide. Regarding Psalm 66:4, in ancient times, a people of the Hebrews was confessing to the one saying to God, 'I am the one who blots out your sins; therefore first confess your sins (uttering them in a manner of repentance) so that you may be justified'—the holy one, bearing the face of this people, says, 'I made my lawlessness known and I did not cover my sin'. But since the arrival of the Savior, all the peoples from the believing nations, being fulfilled, are called to repentance in order to obtain the forgiveness of sins by having confessed to God. How then could it not be a willing following for all the peoples to confess, when the face of God has appeared to them?

Regarding Psalm 66:5, when the way is known in the land and the salvation of God among all the nations, the nations rejoice, having been freed from all evil and the deceit of the many-minded, as they establish moral virtue, and they exult having received the knowledge of God, having learned how the Lord will judge peoples in uprightness and will guide the nations in the land. 'Peoples' and 'nations' are used in a parallel sense: the peoples are those of the circumcision, and the nations are those from the Gentiles.

Regarding Psalm 66:6-7, for how is it not destined that all the earth, that is, the humans upon it, should be filled with praise and bear the fruit of piety, in every place offering incense and pure sacrifice among the nations, as the name of the Lord is magnified, according to what is carried forth in one of the twelve prophets?

Regarding Psalm 67:2, prayer is a word sent forth through imperative words; for instead of 'let him arise' (ἀνασταίη) and 'let them flee' (φύγοιεν), it was written (as 'let him arise' and 'let them flee' in the imperative). For this form is found most continuously in the Scriptures; I mean instead of what is said in a merely direct imperative way. It is possible to say that enemies will be scattered: those who are impious concerning the knowledge of truth, those who hate God, and those who flee from his face having practical wickedness. For if he who loves him keeps...
